seo.metaDescription: Hurt on the job in Stanton? Get a free case review from an attorney who handles workers' comp gaps and third-party injury claims in Orange County.

hero.subtitle: If you were hurt while working in Stanton, our team can review your case at no cost. We understand how Orange County job sites, from warehouses off Beach Boulevard to retail strips near Katella Avenue, generate injury claims that often go beyond a standard workers' comp file.

about.title: Stanton Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Stanton's mix of small industrial yards, retail centers, and delivery routes along Beach Boulevard and Cerritos Avenue means workplace injuries here often involve more than one employer or piece of equipment. California generally requires injured workers to go through workers' compensation regardless of fault, but that system doesn't always cover everything you've lost, and it doesn't apply at all if a negligent third party — a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment manufacturer — caused or contributed to your injury. We review your situation, sort out whether a third-party claim exists alongside your workers' comp case, and explain your options in plain terms. There's no charge for a case review, and no obligation to move forward. If a negligent third party played a role, that information could matter to your recovery.

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Story
items.desc: California generally treats workers' comp as the exclusive remedy against your employer, but if a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker was negligent, a separate third-party claim may be possible.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: California requires you to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate your claim — we can help you understand what's still available.

items.title: Retaliation Protections Exist
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or pursuing a claim, and we can help you understand those protections if you're worried about your job.

items.question: I was hurt on a job site off Beach Boulevard — can I still file a claim if my employer says it was my fault?
items.answer: In California, workers' compensation generally doesn't depend on who was at fault, so an employer's claim of fault usually doesn't block your right to file. If a third party, like a subcontractor or equipment supplier, contributed to the accident, a separate claim against them may also be possible. We can review the specifics and explain your options at no cost to you.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim if a third party caused my injury?
items.answer: Third-party injury claims in California generally carry a two-year deadline from the date of the injury. This is separate from any workers' compensation reporting requirements, which have their own shorter timeline. Because these deadlines can overlap in confusing ways, it helps to talk to us sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I'm afraid my employer will retaliate if I report my injury?
items.answer: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers for reporting an injury or filing a workers' comp claim. If you're concerned about your job security, our team can walk you through your rights before you take any next steps. There's no cost or obligation to have that conversation.
